chapter: Records and playing in New Orleans
title: Recordings with Frank Arnold and the unconcerned family attitude
summary: He made records with Frank Arnold with Smitty and Anderson, never heard them, and says the family just did its own thing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did you make any records, you said?
No. You never? I made several records with, uh, Frank, Frank Trampon, please.
The guy from Germany, Frank Arnold?

Yeah. I made several records with him. Mm-hmm. But I don't know what happened. He and the union had some kind of a little misunderstanding, and he never did get the records or something. He never did get the recordings.

Mm-hmm. And, uh, I don't know what happened, whether it was financial or what, but I know he's able now, but I don't know what happened with that, if you understand. But, uh, we made some nice records. Because I had, we had, uh, Smitty, remember Smitty died piano player? Yeah. He was on there. And, uh, Anderson, trumpet player. Mm-hmm. And, uh, several other guys that was on there that we made the records.
Do you remember the tunes that y'all put up, were gonna have a record? The what? The tunes that y'all were, uh, recalling. Oh, yeah, yeah. Uh-huh.
That one thing. Yeah. Where, uh, here?
No, but the ones that you made, but you never got a chance to see or hear or anything.

I've never had a chance to hear. Because I sing something in that number. You sing in that number? Yeah, I sing a couple of numbers. I don't remember. Because Frank and that, I think it was up on Maple Street where we made those records. Can you recall the way I'm talking about? At somebody's house? Yeah. Didn't Frank used to live on Maple Street or somewhere? They lived on Plum. Plum. That's a pleasant idea. Yeah, uh-huh. Plum or Maple, somewhere else. I think it was Plum. Almost a carol.
I have an idea. Mm-hmm. A house on that side of the street. Mm-hmm. Well, uh...
What were the names of the songs? I can't recall it.
Not even the one you sang on.

You can't remember. No. I know it was the blues and some other number that I sang on. But, uh, we had a lovely time there, you know, playing. Because we always, you know, putting our effort in it. But for me, I mean, I never did worry about if you were recording or doing anything. It's just my daddy taught us to do our thing. If you used to notice Cap, Cap didn't worry about anybody. He didn't worry about it. He just looked like he just took his own and he went on and blew his own. He didn't worry about who was the best, who was better than him, who was greater than him, and all like that. I mean, he didn't worry about anything. And that's the way I am. Sylvester either. Sylvester would put his head on and play his bass. If you like it, it's alright. If you don't, it's alright. Well, that's the way I am. He was liking it. That's right. And so, I mean, uh... You don't try to be the great, you do your thing. Somebody's gonna like it. And, uh... So that's the way we came up playing. We were doing our thing. I think it's one of the greatest things. So, uh... Just like, uh... I went up to the, uh... Head Cap. I think you remember the Head Cap? Uh, Andrew Morgan and the bank of them up there? By your place? And, uh... I just remember whether they recorded or played some numbers up there or what, I know I brought, uh...
